subproblems.title: Mass subadditivity from an evaluation identity Z = X + c·Y with |c| ≤ 1 (parent step 1, F1)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U, G ⊆ ℝ^P be arbitrary sets, let X, Y, Z ∈ 𝒟_n(U), and let c ∈ ℝ with |c| ≤ 1. If Z(ω) = X(ω) + c·Y(ω) for every test form ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ G, then M_G(Z) ≤ M_G(X) + M_G(Y) in [0, ∞]. Conventions: 𝒟_n(U) is the space of n-currents in U (SimonGMT GeometricCurrentOn U n); each of its elements acts ℝ-linearly on 𝒟^n(U). 𝒟^n(U) is the real vector space of test n-forms in U (TestFormOn U n): smooth forms on ℝ^P with compact support contained in U. |α| is the Euclidean coefficient norm of an n-covector α (covectorEuclideanNorm), and |c| is the absolute value of the real number c. M_G(T) = T.massOn G is the supremum in [0, ∞] of ENNReal.ofReal(T(ω)) over the forms ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ G and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x ∈ ℝ^P; this set of forms is massAdmissibleOn U n G, and its elements are called admissible for M_G.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U G : Set (Euclid P)) (X Y Z : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (c : ℝ), |c| ≤ 1 → (∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) ⊆ G → Z ω = X ω + c * Y ω) → Z.massOn G ≤ X.massOn G + Y.massOn G
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 1 (F1) of the parent proof. Simon sums the M-absolutely convergent series R^(ℓ) = Σ_{r≥ℓ} R_r and S^(ℓ) = Σ_{r≥ℓ} S_r in Ch. 6, proof of 7.2 (book/chapter-06.txt lines 2119–2131) without proving this inequality.
The parent's argument: if ω is admissible for M_G then so is ±ω, and ENNReal.ofReal(s + t) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal(s) + ENNReal.ofReal(t). Here the sign ±1 is generalized to a real scalar c with |c| ≤ 1:
- c = 1 gives M_G(A ⊕ B) ≤ M_G(A) + M_G(B);
- c = −1 gives M_G(A − B) ≤ M_G(A) + M_G(B).

Fix P, n, U, G, X, Y, Z and c with |c| ≤ 1. Assume (H): Z(ω) = X(ω) + c·Y(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ G. Write A_G := massAdmissibleOn U n G. By definition, M_G(T) = sSup {ENNReal.ofReal(T(ω)) : ω ∈ A_G} for every T ∈ 𝒟_n(U).

1. (Homogeneity of the coefficient norm.) For every n-covector α on ℝ^P, |c·α| = |c|·|α|.
   By definition |α| = √(Σ_{I : Fin n → Fin P} s_I(α)). Here s_I(α) = (α(e_{I(1)}, …, e_{I(n)}))² if I is strictly increasing and s_I(α) = 0 otherwise, where (e_j) is the standard orthonormal basis of ℝ^P (EuclideanSpace.basisFun).
   Since (c·α)(v) = c·α(v) for every n-tuple v (ContinuousAlternatingMap.smul_apply), s_I(c·α) = c²·s_I(α) for every I. If I is strictly increasing this is (c·t)² = c²·t² (mul_pow); otherwise both sides are 0.
   Summing over I gives Σ_I s_I(c·α) = c²·Σ_I s_I(α) (Finset.mul_sum).
   Since c² ≥ 0, √(c²·Σ_I s_I(α)) = √(c²)·√(Σ_I s_I(α)) (Real.sqrt_mul), and √(c²) = |c| (Real.sqrt_sq_eq_abs).
   Hence |c·α| = |c|·|α|.
2. (c·ω is admissible whenever ω is.) Let ω ∈ A_G.
   TestFormOn U n is a real vector subspace (testFormOnSubmodule), so c·ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) and (c·ω)(x) = c·ω(x) for every x.
   Support: wherever ω vanishes, c·ω vanishes as well, so tsupport(c·ω) ⊆ tsupport ω ⊆ G (tsupport_smul_subset_right).
   Norm: for every x, step 1 gives |(c·ω)(x)| = |c|·|ω(x)| ≤ |ω(x)| ≤ 1. This uses |c| ≤ 1, 0 ≤ |ω(x)| (covectorEuclideanNorm_nonneg) and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 (mul_le_of_le_one_left).
   Hence c·ω ∈ A_G.
3. (Bound at one admissible form.) Let ω ∈ A_G.
   Since Y acts ℝ-linearly on 𝒟^n(U) (Y.toCurrent is a linear map; map_smul), Y(c·ω) = c·Y(ω).
   Since tsupport ω ⊆ G, (H) gives Z(ω) = X(ω) + c·Y(ω) = X(ω) + Y(c·ω).
   Therefore ENNReal.ofReal(Z(ω)) = ENNReal.ofReal(X(ω) + Y(c·ω)) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal(X(ω)) + ENNReal.ofReal(Y(c·ω)) (ENNReal.ofReal_add_le).
   Every admissible evaluation is bounded by the mass (GeometricCurrentOn.le_massOn). So ENNReal.ofReal(X(ω)) ≤ M_G(X) because ω ∈ A_G, and ENNReal.ofReal(Y(c·ω)) ≤ M_G(Y) because c·ω ∈ A_G by step 2.
   Adding the two bounds (add_le_add) gives ENNReal.ofReal(Z(ω)) ≤ M_G(X) + M_G(Y).
4. (Supremum.) M_G(Z) is the supremum of the set {ENNReal.ofReal(Z(ω)) : ω ∈ A_G}. By step 3 every element of this set is ≤ M_G(X) + M_G(Y), so M_G(Z) ≤ M_G(X) + M_G(Y) (sSup_le). ∎
proof_key_steps: Homogeneity: covectorEuclideanNorm(c·α) = |c|·covectorEuclideanNorm(α), since every coefficient square scales by c² and √(c²) = |c|.
If ω is admissible for M_G then so is c·ω: tsupport(c·ω) ⊆ tsupport ω ⊆ G and |(c·ω)(x)| = |c|·|ω(x)| ≤ 1.
For admissible ω, Z(ω) = X(ω) + Y(c·ω) by (H) and linearity. So ofReal(Z(ω)) ≤ ofReal(X(ω)) + ofReal(Y(c·ω)) ≤ M_G(X) + M_G(Y) (ENNReal.ofReal_add_le, GeometricCurrentOn.le_massOn).
Take the supremum over admissible ω (sSup_le).

subproblems.title: Finite partial sums of integer multiplicity currents are integer multiplicity, with subadditive mass (parent steps 1–2)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and U ⊆ ℝ^P. Assume (IS_U): for all integer multiplicity A, B ∈ 𝒟_n(U), the current A − B is integer multiplicity. Let Y_i ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (i ∈ ℕ) all be integer multiplicity. Then for every N ∈ ℕ there is an integer multiplicity Z ∈ 𝒟_n(U) such that (a) Z(ω) = Σ_{i=0}^{N} Y_i(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U), and (b) M_G(Z) ≤ Σ_{i=0}^{N} M_G(Y_i) in [0, ∞] for every set G ⊆ ℝ^P. Conventions: 𝒟_n(U) is SimonGMT GeometricCurrentOn U n and 𝒟^n(U) is TestFormOn U n, the test n-forms in U (smooth forms on ℝ^P with compact support contained in U). Integer multiplicity is the contract predicate IsIntegerMultiplicity. A − B is the contract subtraction (instance Sub on GeometricCurrentOn U n), which acts by (A − B)(ω) = A(ω) − B(ω). M_G(T) = T.massOn G is the supremum in [0, ∞] of ENNReal.ofReal(T(ω)) over ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ G and covectorEuclideanNorm(ω(x)) ≤ 1 for all x. Σ_{i=0}^{N} denotes the sum over Finset.range (N + 1).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (Y : ℕ → GeometricCurrentOn U n), (∀ A B : GeometricCurrentOn U n, IsIntegerMultiplicity A → IsIntegerMultiplicity B → IsIntegerMultiplicity (A - B)) → (∀ i, IsIntegerMultiplicity (Y i)) → ∀ N : ℕ, ∃ Z : GeometricCurrentOn U n, IsIntegerMultiplicity Z ∧ (∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, Z ω = ∑ i ∈ Finset.range (N + 1), Y i ω) ∧ ∀ G : Set (Euclid P), Z.massOn G ≤ ∑ i ∈ Finset.range (N + 1), (Y i).massOn G
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 1–2 of the parent proof. These build the partial sums R^N = Σ_{r=ℓ}^{ℓ+N} R_r and S^N = Σ_{r=ℓ}^{ℓ+N} S_r of Simon's M-absolutely convergent series R^(ℓ) = Σ_{r≥ℓ} R_r, S^(ℓ) = Σ_{r≥ℓ} S_r (Ch. 6, proof of 7.2, book/chapter-06.txt lines 2119–2123). The book asserts that these sums are integer multiplicity without proof.
The parent iterates A ⊕ B := A − ((B − B) − B). This current is integer multiplicity (IM) by (IS), acts as A + B, and satisfies M_G(A ⊕ B) ≤ M_G(A) + M_G(B) by (F1). The parent applies the result with Y_i := R_{ℓ+i} (n = m + 2) and with Y_i := S_{ℓ+i} (n = m + 1); (IS_U) follows from (IS) because U is open.

Fix P, n, U and the family (Y_i). Assume (IS_U) and that every Y_i is IM.

0. (Pointwise subtraction.) For A, B ∈ 𝒟_n(U) and ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U), (A − B)(ω) = A(ω) − B(ω). The contract instance Sub defines A − B as the current whose underlying functional is A.toCurrent − B.toCurrent, so this identity holds by definition.

We prove by induction on N the claim C(N): there is an IM Z ∈ 𝒟_n(U) with Z(ω) = Σ_{i=0}^{N} Y_i(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) and M_G(Z) ≤ Σ_{i=0}^{N} M_G(Y_i) for every G ⊆ ℝ^P.

1. (Base case N = 0.) Take Z := Y_0, which is IM by hypothesis. Σ_{i=0}^{0} consists of the single term i = 0 (Finset.sum_range_one). Hence Z(ω) = Y_0(ω) = Σ_{i=0}^{0} Y_i(ω) for every ω, and M_G(Z) = M_G(Y_0) = Σ_{i=0}^{0} M_G(Y_i) for every G.
2. (Inductive step: set-up.) Assume C(N), witnessed by Z. Put B := Y_{N+1} and Z' := Z − ((B − B) − B) ∈ 𝒟_n(U).
3. (Z' is IM.)
   - B is IM, so B − B is IM by (IS_U) applied to B and B.
   - Then (B − B) − B is IM by (IS_U) applied to B − B and B.
   - Finally Z' = Z − ((B − B) − B) is IM by (IS_U) applied to Z (IM by C(N)) and (B − B) − B.
4. (Evaluation of Z'.) For every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U), step 0 applied three times gives Z'(ω) = Z(ω) − ((B(ω) − B(ω)) − B(ω)) = Z(ω) + B(ω) = Z(ω) + 1·B(ω). By C(N), Z(ω) = Σ_{i=0}^{N} Y_i(ω). Hence Z'(ω) = Σ_{i=0}^{N} Y_i(ω) + Y_{N+1}(ω) = Σ_{i=0}^{N+1} Y_i(ω) (Finset.sum_range_succ).
5. (Mass of Z'.) Fix G ⊆ ℝ^P.
   By step 4, Z'(ω) = Z(ω) + 1·B(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U), in particular for every ω with tsupport ω ⊆ G.
   Apply the sibling mass_triangle (Submission.cmc_fc_sl_massOn_le_add_of_eval_eq) to the sets U and G, the currents Z (as X), B (as Y) and Z' (as Z), and the scalar c = 1, which satisfies |1| = 1 ≤ 1. It gives M_G(Z') ≤ M_G(Z) + M_G(B).
   By C(N), M_G(Z) ≤ Σ_{i=0}^{N} M_G(Y_i). By monotonicity of addition in [0, ∞] (add_le_add), M_G(Z') ≤ Σ_{i=0}^{N} M_G(Y_i) + M_G(Y_{N+1}) = Σ_{i=0}^{N+1} M_G(Y_i) (Finset.sum_range_succ).
6. (Conclusion.) By steps 3–5, Z' witnesses C(N + 1). By induction C(N) holds for every N ∈ ℕ, which is the claim. ∎
proof_key_steps: Induction on N, with base case Z := Y_0 (Finset.sum_range_one).
Inductive step: with B := Y_{N+1}, Z' := Z − ((B − B) − B) is integer multiplicity by three applications of (IS_U).
Pointwise subtraction gives Z'(ω) = Z(ω) + 1·B(ω) = Σ_{i=0}^{N+1} Y_i(ω) (Finset.sum_range_succ).
The sibling mass_triangle with c = 1 and the induction hypothesis give M_G(Z') ≤ Σ_{i=0}^{N+1} M_G(Y_i).
